text:
alex: Heads-up — while validating the CMK rotate scripts I noticed ~20 DB snapshots with an unexpected `OwnerId` mismatch and a null `kmsKeyId` after the last nightly backup run. Could be a tagging/assume-role bug or an actual mis-encrypt to a different key. Need quick triage, possible tenant data exposure on restore. :eyes:

maria: Can you paste the sanitize-ed log/snippet and which region? I can run a targeted inventory.

alex: us-west-2. Snippet from backup-run logs (sanitized):
```
[2026-03-19T02:12:43Z] backup: snapshot create -> snapshot-id: snap-0a1b2c3d4e5f6g7h owner: 123456789012 kmsKeyId: null tag:tenant=acme-prod
[2026-03-19T02:12:46Z] backup: snapshot complete -> snap-0a1b2c3d4e5f6g7h status:completed
```
This specific snapshot should have been encrypted with alias/rdw-prod-cmk.

kate: sec-bot just pushed an alert to #incidents about anomalous restore requests. It correlated to two service accounts that shouldn't have restore perms.

sec-bot: Automated alert: cloudtrail:UnauthorizedRestoreAttempt (2 matches) — resources: [snap-0a1b2c3d4e5f6g7h], triggered by role:svc/backup-runner-prod. See /alerts/18525/alpha.

sebastian: Quick questions: 1) Are snapshots actually unencrypted (SSE disabled) or just missing kmsKeyId metadata? 2) Any customer-facing impact yet?

alex: metadata missing; the S3-backed snapshot chunks are still SSE-KMS encrypted at storage layer for some; but EC2/EBS snapshot metadata shows null kmsKeyId for a subset. No customer restore yet that we know of, but the anomalous restore attempts were blocked by IAM deny.

maria: Probable causes: (A) race in the backup service that created snapshot before CMK attach completed; (B) assume-role used a different account without encryption-permissions so defaulted to unencrypted; (C) bug in our post-create tag/attach step.

ops-jen: If there's any chance a restore could succeed without the right KMS permissions, we should temporarily add an explicit deny on ec2:RestoreSnapshot for non-admin principals and block snapshot-copy-to-different-account flows. I can push that policy in 10m if we decide. :hammer:

kate: +1 on deny. We should also ensure CloudTrail is logging KMS decrypt/encrypt events and forward to SIEM with high-priority rule for kms:Decrypt on snapshots.

maria: Checklist proposal (quick playbook):
1) Freeze restores: add IAM condition deny on ec2:RestoreSnapshot and ec2:CopySnapshot for all non-privileged roles. (ops-jen)
2) Inventory: list all snapshots in us-west-2 with null kmsKeyId and cross-ref owner tag, snapshot age. (maria)
3) Audit trail: ensure CloudTrail trails include DataEvents for KMS and S3 and filter kms:Decrypt events to SIEM. (kate)
4) RBAC review: inspect backup-runner role permissions and the CMK key policy for "Encrypt/Decrypt" across accounts. (sebastian)
5) Short-term re-encrypt: for affected snapshots that are actually unencrypted, create encrypted copy into customer-owned key or our CMK as appropriate. For snapshots with metadata mismatch but stored SSE-KMS encrypted, avoid re-copy until verified. (alex + ops-jen)

sebastian: I'll take RBAC review. Will check backup-runner assume-role chain and the key policy for alias/rdw-prod-cmk. Expect initial findings in ~30m.

maria: Running inventory now: command I'm using
```bash
aws ec2 describe-snapshots --owner-ids 123456789012 --region us-west-2 --query 'Snapshots[?kmsKeyId==`null`].{ID:SnapshotId,Tags:Tags,StartTime:StartTime}' --output json
```
I'll also grep CloudTrail for CreateSnapshot events around 2026-03-19T02:10-02:20Z to see the IAM principal used.

alex: Found one failing call in logs: sts:AssumeRole returned credentials for arn:aws:iam::210987654321:role/backup-exec which is not in our allowlist. That role cannot decrypt with our CMK (policy denies), so snapshot got created without an associated kmsKeyId.

kate: That's a big clue — cross-account assume allowed somewhere. Possibly the role was granted at partner onboarding and overlooked. Need both a fix and a postmortem.

ops-jen: Applying the deny patch to the org SCP/IAM boundary for ec2:RestoreSnapshot and ec2:CopySnapshot for non-admin principals now. Will update when applied.

sec-bot: Change detected: org-policy/update applied by ops-jen at 2026-03-19T02:45:10Z — policy: deny-restore-nonpriv.

ops-jen: Policy pushed. Confirmed denies for the suspect principals.

maria: Inventory result: 23 snapshots with null kmsKeyId, age range 1–3 days. 7 of them are from tenant=acme-prod. I'll export CSV to /shared/sec/18525-snapshot-inventory.csv and share in a follow-up thread.

sebastian: Key policy findings (initial): alias/rdw-prod-cmk had a legacy statement allowing account 210987654321 to "Encrypt" but not "Decrypt". That allowed creation of snapshots encrypted with their key context? Need to fully parse. Will paste JSON soon.

alex: Action items assigned: ops-jen -> deny applied (done). maria -> full inventory + SIEM rule (in progress). sebastian -> RBAC/key policy deep dive (in progress). kate -> update CloudTrail filters and paging alerts to SOC. I'll coordinate customer comms if needed.

kate: For the SIEM rule, use high severity if kms:Decrypt appears for a non-authorized principal or if account != 123456789012 for decrypt on our CMK. Also add rapid paging to oncall.

sebastian: One more note — for any re-encrypt/copy ops we should use the encrypted-copy pattern to avoid exposing plaintext: `aws ec2 copy-snapshot --source-region us-west-2 --source-snapshot-id snap-... --encrypted --kms-key-id alias/rdw-prod-cmk` and block any copy without `--encrypted`.

maria: Agreed. I'll mark snapshots that are actually unencrypted and schedule encrypted copies in a maintenance window after approvals.

alex: Thanks all. Lets do a short postmortem tomorrow and include: why cross-account allowlist existed, why backup-runner assumed the unexpected role, why CMK key policy allowed partial permissions, and how to catch this earlier (pre-flight checks for backup run).

kate: I'll create the incident ticket and link to the inventory and CloudTrail grep. Will include SLA impact (none observed) and mitigation summary.

sebastian: Posting initial key-policy diff here for review (sanitized):
```json
{"Statement":[{"Sid":"LegacyPartnerAccess","Effect":"Allow","Principal":{"AWS":"arn:aws:iam::210987654321:root"},"Action":["kms:Encrypt"],"Resource":"*"}]}
```
We should remove or tighten that to a specific role and deny decrypt/copy.

ops-jen: After the deny, I've also added a short CloudWatch metric to alert on any snapshot create that returns kmsKeyId==null for >0 occurrences in a 15m window.

maria: Good. Tagging follow-ups: @sebastian please propose exact policy changes, @ops-jen keep the deny until postmortem, @kate escalate SIEM rule, @alex draft customer comms if any restores suspected.

alex: Closing here for now — will update when Maria shares CSV and Sebastian posts key-policy PR. :thumbsup:
